finite_dimensional_derivation: For finite-dimensional centralizer A, write φ|A=Σ_i λ_i Tr_i with λ_i>0 and μ=min_i λ_i. Every normalized positive functional ψ|A has density matrices ρ_i with Σ Tr_i ρ_i=1, so ρ_i≤1 and ψ|A≤μ⁻¹φ|A. Therefore ψ∘E_A≤μ⁻¹φ. This does not assume ψ(a)=φ(a yy*).

For φ(y*y)=1, E_A(y*y)≥0 has trace1, norm≤μ⁻¹ and φ(E_A(y*y)^2)≤μ⁻¹. If the source mean-limit argument extends to E_A, the two limiting fourth-moment contributions are bounded by μ⁻¹ and μ⁻¹e^(s+1). Source randomization, polar cutoff and spectral relocalization can then be reused. This is an elementary domination transfer, not claimed substantial.
necessity_derivation: Assume centralizer contains infinitely many nonzero orthogonal p_n and every p_n H p_n has nonzero spectral projection on each nonempty open interval. Select pairwise disjoint intervals I_n→s not containing s and P_n=E_D(I_n)R(p_n). Since p_n is in the centralizer, the spectral and right projections commute; T=ΣP_n is a bounded projection commuting with D.

Unit h_n in P_n H give averaged ||TU_t h_n||²=1. For any uniformly bounded x_j with vector spectral supports shrinking to s, each finite head of T eventually kills x_jξ; the remaining norm is at most ||x_j|| sqrt(φ(Σ_{n>N}p_n)), which tends to zero uniformly as N→∞.

The all-band corner-spectrum assumption still needs the exact Connes typeIII1/state/corner theorem checked in actual primaries. This diagonal concentration mechanism has a strong classical-antecedent risk. Infinite centralizer alone is not enough for arbitrary factors: a diffuse trace has D=0, an isolated spectral point where a fixed bounded witness suffices.
